title: Louisiana's 5th Congressional District Election, 2026
description: Louisiana's 5th Congressional District is an open seat after Republican incumbent Julia Letlow opted to run for the U.S. Senate. A crowded field of candidates from both major parties is competing in what was originally a closed-party primary system, but after the Supreme Court decision in Louisiana v. Callais and subsequent redistricting, Governor Jeff Landry postponed the May 16 primaries and the election is now an open primary on November 3, 2026, with a runoff on December 12 if needed. The district, which stretches from northeast Louisiana down to parts of Baton Rouge, is heavily Republican (Cook Political Report rates it Solid R), and the race features multiple state legislators and political newcomers vying to replace Letlow. The contest has been complicated by legal uncertainty over congressional map boundaries and the switch back to an open-primary format.
polling_note: Only one primary election poll (Rainey Center, April 2026) was publicly available. No general election polls have been released. The primary was postponed after the poll was conducted, so results may not reflect the current candidate field.

candidates.name: Blake Miguez
candidates.summary: Blake Miguez is a Louisiana State Senator representing District 22 and a former state representative. He is a professional marksman, small business owner, and has been endorsed by former President Donald Trump in this race. Miguez initially launched a U.S. Senate campaign before switching to the 5th District race after Julia Letlow entered the Senate contest.

candidates.name: Michael Echols
candidates.summary: Michael Echols is a Louisiana State Representative for District 14 and serves as Chairman of the House Republican Delegation. A real estate developer from Monroe, he has stated he is willing to put $1 million of his own money into the campaign. Echols is considered an ally of Governor Jeff Landry.

candidates.name: Rick Edmonds
candidates.summary: Rick Edmonds is a Louisiana State Senator for District 6 and a former state representative, having served in the legislature since 2016. He is the only Republican candidate living in Baton Rouge, the largest population center in the 5th District, which may give him a geographic advantage. Edmonds emphasizes his experience in state government and infrastructure needs across the district.

candidates.name: Misti Cordell
candidates.summary: Misti Cordell is the Chair of the Louisiana Board of Regents, appointed by Governor Jeff Landry, and is from West Monroe. She has been active in Republican women's organizations and brings experience in higher education policy to the race. Cordell is one of several Republican candidates seeking the open 5th District seat.

candidates.name: Dan McKay
candidates.summary: Dan McKay is an attorney and former prosecutor from Bunkie, Louisiana, running as a Democrat. He describes himself as a conservative Democrat and has emphasized the threat of rural hospital closures, noting that 17 of the 34 rural hospitals at risk of closure are located in the 5th District. McKay supports party primaries and has been critical of the open primary system.

summary_sources.title: Bunkie attorney seeks District 5 seat in Congress

career_history.title: Attorney / Prosecutor
career_history.description: Practices law in Bunkie and has served as a prosecutor.

candidates.name: Jessee Fleenor
candidates.summary: Jessee Fleenor is a dairy farmer from Loranger, Louisiana, running as a Democrat. He describes himself as a Blue Dog Democrat and argues Democrats can compete in the rural 5th District if they are willing to show up and listen to voters. Fleenor emphasizes his agricultural background and commitment to restoring what he calls 'American decency' in politics.

summary_sources.title: Jessee Fleenor says Democrats can still compete in Louisiana's 5th

career_history.title: Dairy Farmer
career_history.description: Operates a dairy farm in Tangipahoa Parish.

candidates.name: Lindsay Garcia
candidates.summary: Lindsay 'Rubia' Garcia is a former educator, legal scholar, and mother of two running as a Democrat. She has been endorsed by prominent Louisiana progressive activist and former U.S. Senate candidate Gary Chambers. Garcia emphasizes a progressive platform focused on people and progress, and has been actively campaigning across the district.

summary_sources.title: Gary Chambers Endorses Rubia Garcia in Louisiana's 5th District Race

candidates.name: Tania Nyman
candidates.summary: Tania Nyman is a community advocate and Democrat running for the 5th District. She has described her candidacy as a 'Newer Deal Democrat' vision rooted in public schools, public services, and democratic control. Nyman has participated in candidate forums across the district alongside fellow Democrats Garcia and Fleenor.

forecast.rationale: Louisiana's 5th District is rated Solid R by Cook and is heavily Republican, giving any Republican nominee an overwhelming structural advantage in this open-seat contest. The lone Rainey Center poll (April 2026) contains no usable matchup data and predates both the primary postponement and the switch to an open-primary format, so polling offers no actionable guidance. The Democratic field (McKay, Fleenor, Garcia, Nyman) faces severe partisan headwinds in a district where Republicans have a massive registration advantage. Among the four Republicans, Blake Miguez is the most plausible frontrunner due to his state Senate profile and endorsement by former President Donald Trump, but the intraparty competition is genuinely uncertain — Echols is a Landry ally with personal wealth, Edmonds has a Baton Rouge base, and Cordell has institutional ties. The safe_r rating reflects near-certain Republican control, but the crowded primary and absence of reliable polling make the specific nominee prediction moderately uncertain.
